symptom: A dynamic-text parameter's customDateFormat holding quoted literal text (`h 'at' mm`) did not round-trip: describe printed `customDateFormat: 'h 'at' mm'`, which ends the string at `h `; and writing 'h ''at'' mm' stored `h ''at'' mm` — in a Java date pattern a literal apostrophe, not the quoted word
cause: Both directions of one property. buildParamFormatV3 stripped the outer quotes with strings.Trim and never unescaped the literal; formatParamFormatSuffix concatenated the stored pattern between quotes instead of calling mdlQuote. The date picker's own CustomDateFormat (input_formatting.go) already used mdlQuote, which is why only the template-parameter path broke
insight: A report that names only the describe half of a string property is worth testing from the WRITE side first: assert the stored value of a statement that contains the escape, before testing describe. Here the store was already wrong, so fixing describe alone would have printed 'h ''at'' mm' and re-stored a doubled pattern — a green-looking change that still loses the value. Any `strings.Trim(x.GetText(), "'\"")` in the visitor is this bug waiting for an apostrophe; unquoteStringLit is the version-aware reader. Revert each half separately: each alone fails the round-trip test
